copy_lock.copy:
This is the kind of love
I want us to grow into.

The date began with one missing key
and two suspects.

By the third wrong turn,
nobody was cute anymore.

“Don’t talk to me.”

He gave her the minute.
Not the distance.

It wasn’t really the wrong turn.

They had simply missed each other
for too many ordinary days.

The plan failed.
The date didn’t.

He still checked the lock twice.
She still rolled her eyes.

Then she went back
and checked it with him.

Prove every locked slide through concrete Aachu/Zuv behavior, not decorative illustration.
Define wants, hidden needs, eye-lines, hands, posture, distance, and joke-to-tenderness movement.
Plan readable text and brandmark placement independently for every request-locked native output.
Translate the selected visual system into specific final-generation and integrated-text constraints.
Select one system only after scoring copy alignment, relationship proof, visual variety, identity, aspect safety, and sendability.

slide_visual_blueprint.copy:
This is the kind of love
I want us to grow into.
slide_visual_blueprint.scene: Rain-damp evening beside a tiny roadside chai stall. Exactly Aachu and Zuv stand under one umbrella beside their modest dark car, safely parked on the quieter service lane away from traffic, dressed for a proper date. Across the divided road, through moving cars, the intended restaurant on the next road is visibly close but inconvenient to reach. The chai stall glows immediately beside them. Aachu points toward the chai stall with her right hand while her left hand stays relaxed at her side. Zuv holds the umbrella in his right hand and lowers the phone map in his left; they exchange a small conspiratorial 'shall we?' look. This is the decision before the accidental date, not the seated payoff. No chai vendor or background people visible.

slide_visual_blueprint.scene: Nonlinear callback to before the date, viewed entirely from OUTSIDE the apartment in a dry corridor after the front door is fully closed. Use a medium-wide, nearly straight-on view of the closed door so the whole action reads without copy. Stage Aachu and Zuv as two separate, non-overlapping figures on opposite sides of the latch zone, with at least one forearm of clear empty space between their torsos: no hug, no waist hold, no leaning against each other, and no couple touch. Zuv stands on the handle side and pulls the single exterior handle with his right hand; his left hand stays naturally hidden behind his own body, and no key is visible in this frame. Aachu has visibly returned from the elevator doors shown deeper in the corridor behind her; both feet and her turned torso point back from the elevator toward the apartment door. Standing separately from Zuv, she extends her right arm across clear open air and presses her fully visible right palm flat on the closed door panel about one hand-width beside the latch. Her fingers, palm, wrist, forearm, and sleeve must remain continuously readable from shoulder to door. Her soft tote hangs from her left shoulder and the tightly rolled bone-dry umbrella rests under her left arm, keeping that hand hidden without covering the focal right arm. Both look toward the door action with small knowing smiles. The two separated bodies, two distinct action arms, closed door, exterior corridor, and visible elevator-return path must make the silent read unmistakable: he tests the handle; she came back and tests the same closed door with him. Their clothes, hair, shoes, umbrella, and corridor floor are completely fresh and dry. Exactly two people. Never show an interior entryway, open door, post-date return, rain marks, Aachu touching Zuv, overlapping torsos, viewer-facing glamour pose, key dangling from the lock, or only one partner checking.
slide_visual_blueprint.must_show: Visible Aachu/Zuv relationship behavior that proves the exact copy.
